(If someone was told that and actually did kill themselves, that is a felony murder charge of some kind.) I frequently have to remind people they can block people, don’t talk about your illness on line, close your account and be very careful who you invite into the new one. No one needs to be harrassed through social media. As people, many of us want/need recognition and look for it on social media. We reveal our whole lives and then complain of no privacy. SM and Tech have their proper uses, but youths are not informed about the bullying, harrassment etc. and how to deal with/avoid it. OK, off the soap box.

questions_and_answers.question: Can technology have negative effects on mental health, such as addiction, stress, and depression, for both children and adults?
questions_and_answers.answer: The biggest issue with technology and all that comes with it is a distraction, and most people are looking for a “distraction” from pressures of modern life. Technology in itself does not cause mental health issues, it just helps provide the “distraction”, and in the process compound underlaying issues. As with all addictions! There is an underlaying issue that needs to be dealt with. How do I know? I work in technology and spend from 8 hours a day to 15 on my laptop/phone. However! I choose times when I DO NOT touch a screen. Two hours from when I wake up are screen free!

questions_and_answers.question: We are often worried about our toddlers getting acquainted with the technology and we don’t want them to get too much attached. Toddlers are at high risk of developing wrong habits and dangerous thoughts in their minds but it is to be noticed that teenagers are at the same risk too. They are also at the developmental age and where we might be able to stop our toddlers from using technology, we can’t do the same with teenagers. So, what can be done? And why is it necessary to be concerned about that? At teenage, when our kids ask to hand them smartphones and let them use social media especially when they are over 13, we can’t say no. This is their age of being up-to-date with the society, to discuss things with their friends, to do what everyone else of their age is doing. If you stop them, they are more likely to do it any way but it will be without your consent and that’s even more dangerous. So, when you are handing them the smartphone, what should be your concerns and how can you tackle them? Teens’ Social Media Use and Mental Health You can’t expect your teen to catch anxiety and depression while using social media, do you? Most of the parents don’t and due to it, they feel that the kids should be left alone with their entertainment and fun. Parents think that if they interfere, it will make their kids go away or feel betrayed. But little do they know that social media has a great impact on the mental health of kids. They are learning a few things from social media that they shouldn’t. They are becoming depressed and anxious day by day due to the things they face on social media. Let’s take a look at the factors on social media that might be playing a strong role in deteriorating the mental health of your teens: Cyberbullying Kids who have faced or are facing cyberbullying are becoming a victim of depression and stress. Where cyberbullying might not be considered a serious issue but it becomes serious when it threatens the life of your teen in multiple ways. Many teens have decided to choose suicide over dealing with such issues. Cyberbullying is a cause for humiliation and harassment in teens. They feel humiliated when they see that they are exposed to the public by someone, and this continues with name-calling, threatening calls, texts, and whatnot. If your kid is suffering through it, you need to help them. Envy No matter how content and satisfied your kid seems to be, when they are on social media, they are not in that mood anymore. Social media is filled with fantasy-based filters and fake life stories. Kids don’t know what is fake and what is not. So, they compare their life with those who have shared fantasy-based life on social media. They feel like they don’t own that glittery life and that their parents have given them nothing. This can easily lead to depression and make them think that it is not the right life for them. Sleep Deprivation Their sleep habits are changing drastically with the use of social media. The more they get into social media, the more they get used to it. If your kid is taking his/her cell phone on the bed, they are probably going to chat, share, comment, and do other multiple things and become sleep deprived. And when you are sleep deprived, you are probably going to face mental health issues that will come to the surface in a while. Addiction If you don’t know it yet, social media addiction is a real thing and it is just like another substance abuse addiction. As they get addicted to social media, they feel the same rush and excitement as anyone with substance abuse disorder would feel. It is as dangerous as that. So, it is obvious that this addiction is going to make their mental health destroyed sooner or later. They lose their grip on reality and make social media their safe place. They usually don’t care what is happening around them when they have their smartphone in their hand. Communication Issues With social media, it is very common that you will get communication issues. At first, they might develop good friendships and relationships, but they realize over time that those relationships aren’t real or worse, they never realize it. While they get used to communicating through texts and chats, they forget how to maintain relationships in real life. Even if they get to meet their online partners in real life, they are seen blank. Communication issues can lead to mental health issues where they can question their confidence and self-esteem. What Should Parents Do? With knowing all this, parents must be concerned about the mental health of their kids. Here are some of the things they can do to make sure it doesn’t come to that point where their kids are suffering from bad mental health: Communicate with them about the danger levels of social media and how it can play with their minds. You need to make sure they know what they are stepping into and how they should treat the difficult things that come their way. Monitoring them is the right option at this point. You need to know what they are up to and how they are dealing with things. You should know how to hack a Facebook account of your kid if you need to view their activity there. By monitoring them, you can know their activities on social media and intervene when it is the right time. Mobistealth is the best monitoring and tracking app that can help you with that. It ensures that you know what your kids are doing and how they are dealing with things. The more you know, the better you can deal with their concerns and take care of their mental health issues. Knowing what your kids are feeling is the biggest benefit for you and you can make sure their mental health is well taken care of. Follow some effective tips on parenting and become a good parent to your kids.

questions_and_answers.question: In recent years, it has become more and more common for teens to use social media. The extent to which teens are using technology has caused extreme concern and distress as to how this overwhelming flow of media will affect their mental health. From playing outside, having face-to-face interactions, and being disconnected from technology, teens now are checking their phones and social media platforms constantly. This makes it complicated to draw the line between online and offline. Teens wake up every morning to check their phones, text their friends and see what others are doing, and most importantly, compare themselves to everything they see online. While there are many benefits to social media, such as self expression, staying in contact with loved ones you cant see everyday, and having easy access to social interaction, the negatives outweigh the positives with social media. Media distorts reality and at a time when teens are growing and finding who they are, being persistently online is hindering their growth and not giving them an accurate representation of real life. At a stage when children are so fragile, social media is causing their emotions to fluctuate with the constant comparison, leading to depression, anxiety, and so many other mental illnesses that are ruining young childrens lives. From the consequences we have seen in past years, psychologists are examining and experimenting with the different effects of social media and looking into the long term outcomes of how much damage it can cause in shaping the adolescent. Based on prior research, psychologists have been able to see the extreme effects of social media on teens and how they are multifaceted and debilitating to the growth of children. While there are many benefits that different apps such as TikTok and Instagram provide us with, like allowing teens to express themselves and maintain other connections with those who they might not be able to see everyday, the negative effects are causing more harm than good to teens. Effects of constant social media use have resulted in increased stress and anxiety, social comparison of others online, depression, isolation and feeling alone, and disruption of sleep. Research has shown that adolescents who use social media at night also face the consequences of feeling anxious and unable to sleep at night. Furthermore, there is a positive correlation between the number of social media accounts one has, with symptoms of anxiety or depression one faces with the constant fear of loneliness and fear of missing out. (Perry) ﻿The growth of FOMO, also known as fear of missing out in children is real, especially with the growth of social media. Teens may see their friends posting online and feel left out, as they are missing pivotal stages of development where friendships are being built. To dive deeper into this term of missing out, children may see a post online and feel the need to compare themselves to others. Not only does social media increase the comparison of teens with what they see online, but it completely skews their perception of reality. This can lead to feeling like they are in competition with friends regarding who can make their lives look better on social media, and a constant feeling of jealousy as to what others may be doing without them. With social media there is a sense of obligation to post things that are socially desirable and fit into a certain standard, one that isnt true. An additional problem we see with the use of social media is cyberbullying. Cyberbullying is worse than ever and is making a huge impact on mental health in our world today. Cyberbullying is arguably one of the most harmful effects of social media because of its ability to reach whoever you want, whenever you would like. While both girls and boys are being bullied online, we see a drastic impact with girls and cyberbullying, with about 42% ﻿of girls ages 13-14, ﻿and 49% ﻿of girls ages 15-17 ﻿have encountered some kind of bullying online in a study from 2022. (Vogels) ﻿Despite these statistical facts, we will never know the true extent of cyberbullying, as not all teens are willing to admit to having been bullied. Whether they feel alone or embarrassed, wanting to reach out or maybe dont know how to ask for help, not all teens are open and willing to share their experiences with cyberbullying. In extreme cases, this constant attack online will result in suicide. Unlike traditional bullying, cyberbullying is done entirely behind the screen, making it hard to see someones initial response to a threat or claim made by a bully. Because cyberbullying has become so prominent overtime, many teens experience hate and feel powerless because of their bullies, who cant see how their actions impact the person they are bullying, because everything is done through a screen. On top of that, since teens have access to their phones 24/7, ﻿cyberbullying is prolonged compared to what used to happen, bullying in school. While bullying in school was unacceptable and detrimental to teens, they would then leave school and move on with their life when they came home. This differs from cyberbullying as it can occur at all times. As stated earlier, in extreme situations, cyberbullying can result in suicide. There has even been a term created based on the emotional toll cyberbullying can have, known as cyberbullicide. This term is used to express the outcome of suicide as a result of cyberbullying. (Schonfeld) ﻿ The effects of cyberbullying are drastic and oftentimes, teens dont know how to reach out when in need. In these cases, this is where harassment online results in the death of a teen. A more recent story is that of a 13 ﻿year old girl named Aubreigh Wyatt. Aubreigh committed suicide because of bullying she received online from four girls who constantly harassed her. Her story has sparked discussions over all social media platforms, being a profound example of cyberbullyings most tragic outcome. People all over have shown support of her and her family as they learn to heal from her disastrous death, using the hashtag #LLAW (Long Live Aubreigh Wyatt). ﻿Her story is heartbreaking, as she received persistent threats online and bullying from her classmates, Aubreigh lost her battle to suicide on Septmeber 4, 2023 ﻿and her family is learning to live without her and bring awareness to her story. (Lee) ﻿This is just one of the numerous cases weve seen where cyberbullying goes too far as to lead to suicide of young boys and girls all over the country. Stories similar to Aubreighs show how much cyberbullying can escalate into overpowering someones life and how urgent it is to spread awareness of cyberbullying and the damage it can do. ﻿Adolescence is an integral stage of life where children and teens are finding themselves, finding their friends, and determining who they will come to be. ﻿Through this stage of life, children seek a sense of belonging and approval from their peers. (Perry) ﻿The addition of social media into children's lives impedes their abilities to grow as individuals and obstructs their ability to emotionally grow and develop, something that is essential to their current state of adolescence. (Girela-Serrano) ﻿As early adolescents are attempting to navigate the various changes in their social environments, they are also experiencing conflict through social media and as a result, experience cyberbullying. (Kim) ﻿Being exposed to social media and feeling the need to conform to others standards delay childrens maturation and encourages comparison and competition between teens. Far too many cases have shown the results of social media and the different impacts it has on teens' mental health and more awareness needs to be brought to this topic to prevent the damage it causes. Suicide is the second leading cause of death of the adolescence in America (Perry) ﻿and recognizing social media's faults and negative aspects is the first step to change and preventing this prevalent issue.
